chunks: If you arrive in Makkah on the Day of Tarwiyah after the sun has set, then there is no mut'ah for you; proceed with your hajj as you are.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The proper way to reconcile these reports is to say that the mutamatti' has a complete 'umrah so long as he reaches the two standings, whether that is on the Day of Tarwiyah, the night of 'Arafah, or the Day of 'Arafah until after zawal. But once the sun has passed the meridian on the Day of 'Arafah, mut'ah has been missed, because he can no longer catch the people at 'Arafat in the manner we described. However, people's ranks differ in merit and reward: whoever reaches on the Day of Tarwiyah at the sun's decline has greater reward and a more complete mut'ah than one who arrives at night, and whoever reaches at night has less reward than that but more than one who arrives on the Day of 'Arafah until after zawal. The reports stating that whoever does not reach the Day of Tarwiyah has missed mut'ah mean the loss of the perfection that he had hoped for by arriving on the Day of Tarwiyah. And what they, peace be upon them, said: 'Let him make it an ifrad hajj,' is directed only to one who strongly expects that if he occupies himself with tawaf, sa'y, exiting ihram, and then entering ihram for hajj, he will miss the two standings. If we carry these reports according to what we have mentioned, we do not discard any of them; this interpretation is indicated by that.
6. What Ibn Abi 'Umayr narrated from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام

about a man who entered into ihram for both hajj and 'umrah together, then arrived in Makkah while the people were at 'Arafat, and he feared that if he performed tawaf and sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah he would miss the standing. So he said: He leaves the 'umrah, and when he completes his hajj he does as 'A'ishah did, and there is no sacrificial offering upon him.
From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Udhafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun's decline past midday, a legal time marker
key_terms.السَّعْيِ: the ritual walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَيْنِ: the two ritual standings, meaning the prescribed standing places of hajj
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: hajj al-tamattu', the form of pilgrimage combining 'umrah and hajj with intervening release from ihram
key_terms.حَجَّةً مُفْرَدَةً: an ifrad hajj, a standalone hajj without tamattu'
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, an important hajj timing marker
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of 'Arafah, central to the rites of hajj

ai.seo_question: Until what point can a pilgrim still perform hajj al-tamattu' before it is considered missed?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal time limit for catching tamattu' in hajj and reconciles differing reports on when the opportunity is considered lost. It explains that the determining factor is whether the pilgrim can still catch the required standings, while also noting varying degrees of completeness and reward depending on how early one arrives.
